resumen: Rahab had hidden the spies on the roof, and their pursuers went out toward the Jordan to look for them. A letter about days of waiting behind a closed gate.

versos.texto: But she had brought them up to the roof, and hidden them under the stalks of flax which she had laid in order on the roof.
The men pursued them along the way to the fords of the Jordan River. As soon as those who pursued them had gone out, they shut the gate.

reflexion: Yesterday Rahab threw the king's men off the trail. Today the story takes us up to the roof of her house. There she had hidden the two spies under the stalks of flax she had laid out. Meanwhile, the pursuers went out along the way to the Jordan, as far as the fords.

And as soon as they had gone out, the gate was shut behind them. They were searching for them far away, while the spies were close by. Hidden under something as simple as a few stalks of flax. But their situation was still delicate: the gate was shut, and they were still inside Jericho.

Sometimes life is like that roof: a hidden place of waiting, not knowing how you will get out. Today you may feel that your gate is closed and that you cannot see the way out. The story does not stay on the roof. It continues in the verses that follow.

God doesn't forget you in the hidden places, or in the days of waiting. You can rest in Him while you wait, and take the next step when the time comes. And if the waiting feels heavy, talk about it with someone you trust or with a professional: that, too, is part of care.
dedicatoria: This letter is for you, who are waiting behind a closed gate. God has not forgotten you.
oracion: Lord, in the days of waiting, remind us that we are not alone. Give us patience and trust when we cannot see the way out. In Jesus' name, amen.
